item.title: Lewis Hamilton's Gaza Instagram posts draw scrutiny after visit to Egypt's Rafah Crossing border
item.description: Lewis Hamilton visited Egypt's Rafah Crossing and condemned Israel's actions in Gaza as "genocide," but critics noted the walls he referenced.
item.content:encoded:
Ferrari Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton is not one to shy away from politics, but his recent Instagram posts have raised some eyebrows.

According to Reuters, the seven-time world champion visited El Arish, Egypt, where he was briefed on humanitarian efforts in Gaza.

He also took some time to visit the Rafah Crossing, which is the gateway between Egypt and Gaza.

FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

There, Hamilton took some photos, which were accompanied by a caption in which he condemned Israel's "genocide" in Gaza.

"The past three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza are appalling," Hamilton wrote. "It’s an injustice for people to being denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.

'NOBODY WANTS THIS' STAR ACCUSES ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE'

"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help."

Of course, many were quick to point out that the walls Hamilton was looking at were on the Egyptian border with Gaza.

He talked about seeing lines of vehicles at the crossing there to deliver aid, and then once again took another direct swipe at Israel.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in," he wrote. "No excuse."

LEWIS HAMILTON, WORTH $500M AND DATING BILLIONAIRE KIM KARDASHIAN, WANTS TO PUT 'A LIMIT' ON WEALTH

OutKick has reached out to both Scuderia Ferrari and the team's title sponsor, HP, for comment on Hamilton's posts, but has yet to hear back.

Hamilton is not afraid to discuss off-track issues, and he even brought them on track at times. At certain races with Mercedes between 2021 and 2024, including in the Middle East in nations like Qatar and Saudi Arabia, he wore a pro-LGBTQ helmet.

Formula 1 is off this week following the Brazilian Grand Prix, but will be back in action next week when the series heads to Las Vegas.

item.title: Democrats eye killing Senate filibuster as lawmaker warns move could be a 'double-edged sword'
item.description: Ed Markey says the filibuster must be "on the table" as Democrats take the Senate, while Andy Kim warns the move could be a "double-edged sword."
item.content:encoded:
Democratic senators are leaving the door open to eliminating the Senate filibuster as their party prepares to take control of the chamber, with one lawmaker saying the move must be on the table while another warned it could be a "double-edged sword."

"Obviously, the filibuster is something that has to be on the table," Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., told Fox News Digital when asked about Democrats' plans for the chamber.

But Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., warned that changing the rules could carry consequences long after Democrats leave power.

SCHUMER, JEFFRIES SIDESTEP QUESTIONS ON NUKING FILIBUSTER, LAUNCHING ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER BLUE WAVE

"Some of these things that we see here can be very much a double-edged sword," Kim said. "I'm not saying that's to deter us from doing it if we decide to do it. But I wanna make sure that everyone's clear-eyed about what we're doing."

Scrapping the Senate's 60-vote hurdle would allow Democrats to advance most legislation with a simple majority, weakening Republicans' ability to block their agenda — but also giving the GOP the same advantage if it regains control.

Fox News Digital pressed the senators on whether Democrats would consider changing the rules while President Donald Trump remains in office or wait until a potential Democratic presidential victory in 2028.

"We're discussing a progressive agenda right now and amongst the other Democratic senators," Markey said. "So I'll be listening to everyone's views on what is the best strategy."

SCHUMER'S GRIP ON POWER SLIPS AS DEMS BEGIN TO REVOLT AGAINST HIM, EYE NEW LEADERSHIP

Trump pressed Senate Republicans to abolish the filibuster when trying to pass the SAVE America Act, warning that Democrats would eliminate it if the party took back the majority — and now they have.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., stayed silent when asked if he would support Democrats getting rid of the filibuster if they win the White House in 2028. Schumer is currently under scrutiny from progressives as the party considers who will lead the Senate after winning back the majority.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., announced Thursday that he will be running against Schumer for Senate Majority Leader and is in favor of terminating the filibuster, even going as far as characterizing it as "anti-democratic."

"My personal view has been all along that the filibuster is an anti-democratic … provision. It's not in our Constitution," Van Hollen said. "It was put in there by senators to enhance their power over the power of the people."

SCHUMER FACES MUTINY FROM NEWLY ELECTED SENATE DEMS AS PARTY PREPARES TO SEIZE POWER

Kim cautioned that changing Senate rules could set a precedent Democrats might later regret.

"When you open the door…you gotta be ready," Kim said. "You don't wanna shoot from the hip when it comes to really big issues that are affecting our country in this way."

He suggested pushing legislation "through other means" before jumping to nuking the filibuster.

"I think we as a caucus would need to think through…what would we want to pass such that that would be an obstacle, you know, and I think we should be pushing as much as we can through other means," Kim said.

item.title: Bari Weiss at CBS News: A year of drama and challenges as she attempts to revamp the Tiffany Network
item.description: Bari Weiss' first year as CBS News editor-in-chief brought newsroom clashes, "60 Minutes" firings and a continuous ratings decline of its newscasts.
item.content:encoded:
It has been a tumultuous year for CBS News as the network has been rocked by ownership changes and a polarizing new boss.

Last October, then-newly minted Paramount owner David Ellison tapped Bari Weiss as editor-in-chief of CBS News as part of his $150 million purchase of her outlet The Free Press.

What has unfolded over the past year is a revolving door of talent, newsroom clashes and a continuous ratings decline.

BARI WEISS BEING NAMED TOP CBS NEWS EDITOR CAUSES LIBERAL MEDIA TO MELTDOWN

The battle lines seemed to have been drawn even before Weiss stepped foot inside the CBS newsroom. Her appointment came on the heels of Ellison's $8 billion takeover of Paramount, which critics believe only received the FCC's blessing after Paramount settled President Donald Trump's "60 Minutes" lawsuit for $16 million. Ellison and his billionaire father, Larry Ellison, are perceived as having a cozy relationship with Trump, fueling fear among liberals that he would turn CBS News into MAGA TV.

Weiss, who launched The Free Press following her dramatic exit from The New York Times, had been branded by her critics as an anti-woke conservative despite having more heterodox views. When she was appointed by Ellison, she quickly embraced his mission to appeal to the "70%" in the political center rather than the fringes on the left and right.

Still, that hasn't stopped outlets such as the left-wing blog The Daily Beast from branding the new CBS chief as being "MAGA-coded."

Weiss has been a very hands-on editor according to multiple leaked reports, some of which spiraled into contentious newsroom battles.

Her first big clash came last December with Sharyn Alfonsi, then a "60 Minutes" correspondent who was set to air a report on the notorious El Salvador prison CECOT but was temporarily shelved at the last minute by Weiss. Weiss insisted at the time that the report wasn't ready and that it needed a voice from the Trump administration, while Alfonsi accused her of playing politics. Liberal critics attacked Weiss, alleging she was trying to censor a report critical of Trump. The segment ultimately aired in January.

BARI WEISS FACED 'SIGNIFICANT RESISTANCE' FROM CBS NEWS STAFFERS ABOUT ALASKA BALLOT SCANDAL, INSIDERS SAY

Last month, Status reported that Weiss had clashed with veteran correspondent Lesley Stahl during the editing process of a "60 Minutes" segment about Israeli settler violence in the West Bank. The dispute allegedly became so heated that Stahl "privately floated" quitting. A CBS spokesperson called the report "ludicrous."

According to Semafor, two CBS News staffers were reportedly upset when Weiss urged journalists to investigate the Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's alleged family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood when the controversy erupted. Additionally, a leaked recording from a meeting captured CBS News correspondent Holly Williams having a heated exchange with Weiss' hand-picked foreign editor Shayndi Raice over the network's coverage of Israel and the Oct. 7 terrorist attack, with Raice invoking "legal grounds for firing" and "insubordination" if staff didn't fall in line with the top brass.

Anonymous CBS News employees have frequently aired complaints about Weiss to media reporters during her tenure.

CBS BOSS FUELS LEFT-WING UPROAR AMID REPORT SHE URGED STAFF TO PROBE ALLEGED EL-SAYED, MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES

Perhaps the most affected CBS News program under Weiss has been "60 Minutes."

In May, the network shocked the media landscape when it announced several firings, including "60 Minutes" executive producer Tanya Simon and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. Weiss also tapped documentary filmmaker and former New York Times columnist Nick Bilton to replace Simon as the show's top producer.

CBS NEWS FIRES '60 MINUTES' CORRESPONDENTS, TOP PRODUCER IN SWEEPING SHAKEUP OF STORIED PROGRAM

Tensions further escalated when veteran correspondent Scott Pelley lashed out against Bilton and Weiss at an all-staff meeting days later, where he accused Weiss of "murdering" the storied newsmagazine program and bluntly told Bilton, who has no linear television experience, that he had "slender qualifications" for his new role. That led to Pelley's own termination.

With the exit of Anderson Cooper in February, "60 Minutes" suddenly lost four of its seven correspondents.

SCOTT PELLEY FIRED AT CBS NEWS AFTER BLOWUPS WITH BARI WEISS, NEW '60 MINUTES' PRODUCER

Weiss and Bilton announced in July that they had poached New York Times columnist Ross Douthat and tapped CBS veteran Norah O'Donnell as new "60 Minutes" correspondents, along with several contributors who would join Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim.

Despite all the reported drama, the new season of "60 Minutes" has closely resembled the program viewers have been used to, except for minor cosmetic changes to graphics and the new personalities leading the reports. And while the show nabbed big exclusives — including interviews with the Air Force service member who was rescued out of Iran earlier this year and the ex-husband of Lindsay Clancy — it didn't result in any major ratings bump as trend lines continue to be unfavorable to "60 Minutes."

BARI WEISS POACHES CONSERVATIVE NY TIMES COLUMNIST, OTHERS JOIN '60 MINUTES' IN CBS PROGRAM SHAKEUP

"60 Minutes" isn't the only program to have undergone personnel changes. "CBS Evening News" co-anchors John Dickerson and Maurice DuBois exited the network after just a year at the desk.

Weiss handpicked the "CBS Mornings" co-host Tony Dokoupil to lead the evening newscast. His debut was a bit bumpy between being marred by technical difficulties and raised eyebrows for his lighthearted "salute" to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. One of his top producers was also dismissed just days into the show's reboot.

Filling Dokoupil's seat alongside Gayle King and Nate Burleson on "CBS Mornings" is Norah O'Donnell, who previously co-hosted what was then called "CBS This Morning" from 2012 to 2019.

Weiss also poached Matt Gutman from ABC News as a top correspondent for the network while CBS News reporter Scott MacFarlane headed for the exit.

NORAH O'DONNELL URGES LIBERAL BARI WEISS CRITICS TO GIVE 'CBS MORNINGS' A CHANCE AS SHE RETURNS TO PROGRAM

For decades, CBS News has been the perpetual third-place broadcaster behind its rivals ABC and NBC. So it was a Herculean task for Weiss to turn things around, especially in just one year.

"CBS Mornings" is on pace to have its worst year ever, down to an average of 1.7 million viewers — a 12% drop from last year. That's far below the average 2.9 million and 2.8 million that tune in to "Today" and "Good Morning America" respectively.

"CBS Evening News" similarly came in a distant third with its 4 million average viewers, less than half of the 8.3 million who watch "World News Tonight with David Muir" and well behind 6.5 million viewers who watch "NBC Nightly News w/ Tom Llamas." The program did, however, close October with a 16% bump from October 2025.

The Tiffany Network's strongest performer, at least in direct competition with its rivals, is its marquee Sunday show "Face the Nation," maintaining its modest lead with 2.9 million average viewers, while ABC's "This Week" and NBC's "Meet The Press" average 2.69 million and 2.5 million respectively, though "Meet The Press" does lead among viewers in the advertiser-coveted demo ages 25-54 while "Face The Nation is second in that metric.

"60 Minutes," meanwhile, had its lowest-rated October performance since at least 2000, despite remaining CBS News’ most-watched show.

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

Weiss has had a challenging first year, and year two may have its own challenges as Paramount's parent company, Skydance, begins integrating all the properties from its $111 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, which includes CNN.

Rumors of Ellison elevating Weiss to a role overseeing both CBS News and CNN have been put on ice for now. Industry critics remain speculative as to what Ellison has in store for his two news operations as he explores ways to cut costs throughout the company.

A spokesperson for CBS News declined to comment.

Fox News' Brian Flood contributed to this report.

item.title: UFC ring announcer Bruce Buffer, 69, has no plans of retirement any time soon; wants 'to keep going'
item.description: Bruce Buffer says he plans to keep announcing UFC fights for at least another decade, with his sights set on UFC 400 and no retirement in sight.
item.content:encoded:
There's no need to worry about when Bruce Buffer is going to retire.

The 69-year-old has been the in-ring announcer for UFC since 1996 and became full-time the following year, and as the company's popularity has grown, so has his superstardom.

He's been in the ring for thousands of fights at hundreds of major events all over the globe, but there are no signs of stopping.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"That seems to be a question I get a lot these days," Buffer said when recently asked by OutKick how much longer he plans on working.

"I still got it. Unless everybody wants me to leave—and I understand — but I plan on being here. I told everybody I’m looking forward to UFC 400. That doesn't mean I'm going to retire [then]. I can’t stand still. I physically and mentally put every ounce of energy I can into every night at work."

For those counting at home, with one major UFC event monthly, that would take place in the summer of 2031. But before that, his next duty is UFC 344 at Madison Square Garden on Saturday night with what is a stacked card in front of "hardcore fight fans."

But that role is not without double-dipping in Bud Light's new campaign as a steak waiter amid the release of the beer brand's "Fight Night Feast," which features official UFC gloves, two tomahawk steaks, a Paramount+ subscription to watch the fights and, of course, Bud Light.

"It sounds like a perfect night," Buffer said.

"I’ve always loved being self-deprecating, as they say. I love humor, and I love poking fun at myself. When Bud Light came to me, showed me the storyboards and we talked about it, I thought, 'Oh, this is going to be fun. I could definitely get into this one.' I have no problem being funny and doing whatever it takes," Buffer said of his acting skills in the new ad.

UFC BOSS DANA WHITE BRUSHES OFF DEMOCRATIC PROBE THREATS, RECALLS 'CRAZY 48 HOURS' AROUND TRUMP JOB OFFER

That was a different world for Buffer, but he'll be in his normal surroundings on Saturday night, and many more Saturday nights afterward.

"I plan on doing this for at least another 10 years," Buffer said.

But despite being his normal, longtime gig, he certainly doesn't treat it as such.

"Every night is my very first night. I have to prove to myself, the fans, the powers that be, Dana White, you, and the fighters that I deserve this job," Buffer said. "I want to go home knowing I deserve it. When I come out tomorrow night, Saturday night, that’s my first night. I don’t live on my laurels.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"I’m 69 now, but I’ve been an athlete my whole life. I train and want to keep going. I work around the greatest athletes in the world. They keep me going."

item.title: Five college football bets for Saturday, including two road dogs that are being slept on
item.description: College football Week 11 best bets feature road underdogs, opportunities to fade the public and picks for Saturday’s biggest matchups.
item.content:encoded:
Week 11 is where the college football calendar starts to separate the contenders from the pretenders. The College Football Playoff committee has shown its hand with a few rounds of controversial rankings, but teams now know exactly what they’re playing for. That doesn’t always show up in the point spread.

Some teams are chasing a seed. Others are protecting one, and a few are just trying to get to the finish line with their pride and coaching staff intact. Miami is coming off its first loss of the season. Tennessee is trying to justify a top-eight ranking on the road and South Carolina is staring down a visit from Georgia next week. Spots like these are where lines get shaded toward the brand name and away from what’s happening on the field.

That’s where I’m looking this week. Over the past month, the board has priced in reputation more than results, and it’s created some value worth chasing. Two of these plays are road underdogs most bettors won’t touch, and a third is a home dog getting points from a ranked team that hasn’t proven much away from Knoxville.

CFP REACTION: ALABAMA FEELS THE LOVE, INDIANA GETS THE SHAFT AND BIG 12 GETS RELIEF AS COMMITTEE CONFUSES US

Here are my five best bets for Saturday.

This line opened higher and has slid to 7.5, so the market is cooling on the Gamecocks. I’m happy to buy at the lower number.

No. 17 South Carolina has won four straight. Arkansas is 3-6, 1-5 in SEC play, and won’t be going bowling in Ryan Silverfield’s first season. With South Carolina, Texas and LSU to close the year, the Razorbacks are mostly playing out the string.

LaNorris Sellers is playing through a sore ankle, which could mean fewer designed runs this week. Against this Arkansas defense, that shouldn’t matter much.

Georgia coming to town next week creates a lookahead angle, and I understand the concern. But a team that has won four in a row with a playoff path still in front of it shouldn’t sleepwalk through a road trip to a 3-6 opponent.

The pick: South Carolina -7.5 (-112)

Wake Forest is a road underdog against an unranked team, and that’s hard to square with how well this team has played. I understand, people still don't believe in this team, but I believe in them enough in this spot.

The No. 13 Demon Deacons have outscored their last five opponents 264-31, which is remarkable in any conference. They rank first nationally in EPA per play, have covered seven straight and are an ACC-best 7-2 against the spread.

The case for SMU is they are extremely stingy at home. The Mustangs are 11-0 at home in ACC play since joining the league, and Kevin Jennings has been much better at home than on the road. But SMU has allowed 28 points in back-to-back games, and Wake’s offense has been scoring at will.

I love Wake's offense against this SMU defense right now.

The pick: Wake Forest +1.5 (-115)

Texas Tech is ranked No. 12, and Oklahoma State only just made the CFP Top 25. The rankings point one way, and the matchup points the other.

Oklahoma State’s offense ranks second in the FBS in total yards. Texas Tech’s defense ranks 110th in total defense and 136th against the pass, near the very bottom of the sport. Drew Mestemaker also gets a standalone night game on ESPN, a national stage that can only help his Heisman and draft stock.

The Red Raiders have been out-gained in every road game this season. A 73.5 total tells you points are expected, and Oklahoma State is the team better built to win that kind of game.

I’m passing on the 3.5-point spread and taking the moneyline. I just need the Cowboys to win.

The pick: Oklahoma State ML (-170)

First thing's first, I'll take any edge I can get. And the Tennessee football team was caught up in the nationwide grounding of planes last night. I liked the Aggies before I learned of the Vols' travel issues. Tennessee is No. 8 and laying points on the road against a 4-5 team. The public has seen that number and hammered the Volunteers early. I’m going the other way.

Tennessee’s last win deserves a closer look. The Vols beat Kentucky 34-6, but it was 13-6 entering the fourth quarter and the yardage was dead even. They also lost their last road game, at South Carolina. Seventeen of their 24 home touchdowns came against Missouri State, Arizona State and The Citadel. Not exactly a group of juggernaut defenses.

The Aggies have been more unlucky than bad. In a 17-9 loss to South Carolina, they had 26 first downs and 457 yards without a turnover. Marcel Reed has struggled as a pocket passer this season at times, but with Holmon Wiggins now calling plays, expect Reed to get out and use his legs more.

The concern is real. Tennessee leads the nation with 39 sacks, and Reed completes fewer than half his passes under pressure. Still, a home dog playing its first SEC home game in over a month is the right side of this number. Gig 'em.

The pick: Texas A&M +2.5 (-105)

NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF POLL PROVES THE SELECTION COMMITTEE IS JUST MAKING IT UP AS THEY GO

This is my favorite bet on the card.

Manny Diaz is a Miami native who was fired by the Hurricanes after three seasons. Now he brings Duke back to his old building, and he’s 12-4 against the spread as a road underdog in his career. Games like this tend to mean a little more. Darian Mensah facing his former team adds another revenge layer for the Blue Devils.

Miami leads the nation at 45 points per game, but the offense hasn’t been the same without receiver Malachi Toney. The Hurricanes are also coming off their first loss of the season, albeit a controversial one, 31-24 to Notre Dame. Duke’s defense allows 13 points per game, fifth in the country, and has held five of nine opponents to single digits.

Nearly two touchdowns is a lot of points to give against a defense this good and I think Duke is very much in this game in the late going.

The pick: Duke +13.5 (-108)

Odds via DraftKings and subject to change.

item.title: Lane Kiffin owes LSU fans more than hype as Texas threatens to bury $40 million playoff dream
item.description: Arch Manning and No. 6 Texas head into Tiger Stadium for a Saturday showdown that could officially end LSU's playoff hopes under Lane Kiffin.
item.content:encoded:
BATON ROUGE, La. — LSU and its boosters paid for the roster. The fans bought the tickets and into the hype. Now it’s time for Lane Kiffin to deliver a signature win.

Just outside of Tiger Stadium on a Friday afternoon, the expensive RV's started making their way into the coveted spots that will host a full day of tailgating before the showdown against No. 6 Texas that is a must-win for an LSU team on the brink of playoff elimination.

The pressure of a game that will determine whether Kiffin faces a very long offseason of reflection was not part of the story some envisioned just two months ago, when potential Tigers sat inside a Baton Rouge courtroom trying to convince a judge to let them join a football team practicing just a few miles away.

LANE KIFFIN HITS DEATH VALLEY WITH SHAQ, PAUL SKENES, ANGEL REESE AND, NATURALLY, KEVIN COSTNER

We got to this point thanks to a 31-13 beating that came at the hands of Alabama last weekend in this same town, which sent fans into a frenzy around the prospects of not making the postseason.

I don't think anyone could rationally say that they expected Lane Kiffin to win a national championship in his first season as head coach at LSU.

I would wholeheartedly agree that the Tigers should not be in this current predicament with a roster that costs over $40 million, and a coaching staff that hovers around $100 million in total.

People are watching, though, whether that be to see the downfall of Kiffin or who he gets off the bus with for the Tiger Walk into a historic stadium that has been home to a number of letdowns in recent years for an LSU team that was the talk of this offseason.

Oh, and if you think the hype for this football squad came from those outside the state of Louisiana, you might need to check the press clippings. LSU knew exactly what is was doing in every move made that started with Kiffin boarding a private jet in Oxford last December.

There will be no sympathy given for a football program that has seen Governor Jeff Landry and President Wade Rousse stoke the flames of this Kiffin era in Baton Rouge. But, it's not as if LSU officials are looking for it, though.

Every person associated with the buildup to this 2026 season played a part in where we currently sit, with Texas looking to come into Tiger Stadium and put the final nail in this first-year coffin.

It also just happens to be Louisiana native Arch Manning that will get off the bus on Saturday evening and walk into a hostile crowd in hopes of sending this fan base into a full-blown meltdown.

Remember, though, LSU wanted to be the villains in this cinematic experience that we have witnessed play out over the past eleven months. But, if there ever was a time for the bad guys to get a win over the babyface, that would be tonight against a Texas team looking to clinch its own spot in the CFP.

"Nope, I surely didn’t think this would be the case," Andy, from New Orleans, told OutKick. "Don't get me wrong, Kiffin will win at LSU with the resources he has at his disposal. Well, he better win with that amount of money, I should say.

"It's year one, things happen. But if you're asking if I'm frustrated that we have three losses and Alabama tore us up in the fourth quarter last week, sure I am. Look at all the other teams that are struggling though. Heck, Ohio State got destroyed last week. Texas A&M wasted all that money on its roster. And, I've already been hit up for donations in 2027. We're in this for the long haul, but we could use a big win tonight."

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S MEGA ROSTERS AREN’T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON PROVE

The tents were being setup on Friday afternoon, a lot of them with Raising Cane's signage that is scattered throughout the tailgate scene.

If you're wondering why, that would center around owner Todd Graves being a major donor for the LSU athletic department. The money that was needed to piece together this expensive 2026 roster, a nice chunk of that came from the guy who has perfected the chicken tenders chain that continues opening stores across the country.

But, there were plenty of other significant donations made by boosters with ties to the LSU program who are looking for a return on their investment. It's not as if the Tigers can just use local hospitals or something to increase their revenue pool, Kiffin has to do his part in raising the money needed to compete.

Now, that comes more by telephone than actual donor retreats or a weekly sit-down with influential people with money to spend.

In most cases, though, the financial part of LSU's football program comes from the love each booster has for a program with such a rich tradition, even if they have to watch highlights of the 2019 season to fill their cup as of late.

Saturday night, the Tigers will take to the field in Baton Rouge for the final time this season in hopes of keeping their playoff hopes alive. A win against No. 6 Texas would be the first part. Next week, LSU travels to No. 8 Tennessee in what has the chance to be a dangerous atmosphere that could also be for a spot in the CFP (Vols need to beat Texas A&M).

The final act would come against an Arkansas team that has struggled to look competitive for most of this season.

If, and that's a big if, LSU can win the next three games to conclude the regular season, they will have a very strong argument for making the playoff with three losses.

ALABAMA FINALLY PUTS IT ALL TOGETHER, DOMINATES LSU AND LEAVES LANE KIFFIN STARING AT $40 MILLION CFP DISASTER

But, with Steve Sarkisian leading this Texas football team into Tiger Stadium with a ferocious defense and Arch Manning having more of a swagger to him, the Longhorns could add fuel to the already simmering nightmare that would have LSU participating in a meaningless bowl game around New Years Eve.

After last week's gut-wrenching loss to Alabama, it's time for Lane Kiffin to provide LSU fans with an early Christmas present to thank them for helping fund his new life in Baton Rouge.

If he doesn’t, I'd imagine a few bags of coal will somehow appear on his doorstep this holiday season, and there might not be much to be thankful for when the Turkey is taken out of the oven in two weeks.

Tiger fans are searching for more than just social media clicks and red-zone execution excuses from their football program.

They expect a win tonight.

item.title: Clown Desmond Howard takes a disgusting shot at Jeremiah Smith, buy Melania's swimsuit & Butler Blue V debuts
item.description: Desmond Howard questioned when Jeremiah Smith has been the difference in big games, igniting fury among Ohio State fans during Heisman voting season.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun.

Never forget how this loser acted towards CJ Stroud during the 2021 Heisman ceremony. Never forget the completely one-sided analysis that he provides when it comes to anything related to Ohio State. And now you should never forget that this is how this loser talks about Jeremiah Smith.

"When in the last two seasons has Jeremiah Smith been the difference in big games?" this loser asked during a Friday hit on ESPN.

OHIO STATE'S JEREMIAH SMITH IS NOW THE HEISMAN FAVORITE FOLLOWING HISTORIC PERFORMANCE

What's this all about? Heisman voting and trolling Ohio State fans when Michigan is headed for a historically terrible season. Desmond doesn't want Smith anywhere near the Heisman Trophy. It's all he has to live for this college football season.

Smith only went for eight catches, 164 yards and a touchdown against Texas earlier this year. In October, on the road at then No. 14 Iowa, he only went for 11 catches, 206 yards and two touchdowns.

He had the go-ahead touchdown last year at Michigan to bury those losers. He had eight catches for 144 yards against Indiana in the B1G championship game. He had seven catches, 157 and a touchdown against Miami in the playoffs.

During the 2021 Heisman ceremony, which should have been one of Stroud's proudest moments, Howard made sure to make the Ohio State quarterback the butt of his joke while Desmond was glazing Michigan Man Aidan Hutchinson.

"Better than his offensive linemen," Howard said after Tim Tebow commented about Kenny Pickett keeping the peace between Stroud and Hutchinson on the Heisman stage.

item.title: Dems descend on Denver to size up 2028. We asked who wants in the race
item.description: Josh Shapiro, Elissa Slotkin, Cory Booker and Ruben Gallego tested 2028 messaging at a Denver conference as Chris Van Hollen bowed out early.
item.content:encoded:
DENVER — Democrats are already making their case for 2028.

Fresh off sweeping midterm victories, party leaders and rising stars descended on Denver for the "What’s Next" conference. Several potential presidential contenders tested their 2028 messaging before a crowd of activists, strategists and operatives.

The conversations offered an early look at who may be considering a run and who is already stepping aside.

Less than 24 hours after announcing a challenge to longtime Senate Democratic leader Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., told reporters he was "no longer pursuing" a presidential bid.

SCHUMER'S LEADERSHIP RIVAL REVEALS MAJOR SENATE RULE CHANGE HE'D PURSUE IF ELECTED

"I believe that the size and scale of these majorities, provides an opportunity for the United States Senate to answer the call of the American people," Van Hollen told reporters in Denver, as he pointed what will be at least a 55-seat Democratic majority in the chamber.

Van Hollen’s comments came as Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., weighed whether to make another run for the White House in 2028.

Booker said he is giving "a lot of hard thought" to a potential 2028 presidential campaign, though he said his focus now is pushing for what he called an "American renewal."

"My purpose right now, I want to see America in the next five years have the biggest renewal, the biggest resetting of the economic table so it works for all Americans," Booker told Fox News Digital.

He pointed to the cost of housing, healthcare and childcare as evidence that many Americans are struggling to get ahead. "The gap I’m concerned about is not the gap between left and right anymore, it’s a gap between the American people and the American dream, and I want to see that gap close," he said.

Asked what he might do differently if he ran again after his unsuccessful 2020 campaign, Booker said candidates should be "their authentic self." He also warned that political divisions are pulling the country apart, saying, "We are not each other’s enemies. We are our fellow patriots. And we all need to start pulling in the same direction."

While Van Hollen ruled out a presidential bid, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, a 2020 Democratic candidate, told reporters in Denver he would not have "any news to make about that anytime soon."

Even so, Buttigieg has not ruled out another run.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, fresh off of major victories in his home state, said, "I've decided to be a loud voice in this process that we're going through right now as a party to put ourselves in the best position to compete."

When asked about his 2028 timeline, Shapiro said "that would be a personal decision my wife and my kids and I make."

"When we're ready to say something, we'll let you know," he added.

Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan told reporters that she was "seriously" considering a 2028 presidential run.

"I haven't made any decisions. Whether it's me or somebody else, I just want to be a part of that next generation of leaders going forward that does things differently and understands who they serve," she added.

Pointing to a new crop of Democrats elected in the midterms, Slotkin said "we had an amazing election night that elected a whole bunch of new folks who represent that."

Meanwhile, Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona said his young family will be a major consideration in his decision.

"I have three kids, nine, three and a one-year-old. You know, it's hard to manage that schedule and I have to figure out how to still be a good dad and run for office," he said.

"If I run I'll probably be the only one that has kids that age that doesn't necessarily come from a lot of money. So I'm going to have to figure all that out," he added.

THE MISTAKE NEWLY ELECTED DEMS ADMIT THEY CAN’T AFFORD TO MAKE WITH TRUMP AFTER SWEEPING 2026 WINS

Sen. Raphael Warnock, D-Ga., who has not said whether he will seek the 2028 nomination, used his speech at "What's Next" to argue Democrats can build a winning coalition across the country.

"In America, all things are possible," he said, pointing to Democratic victories from New Hampshire to Mississippi.

California Rep. Ro Khanna said he is "certainly considering" a 2028 presidential run but has not made a decision.

Khanna, one of the few leaders on the progressive left attending a conference organized by a centrist Democratic group, added "I think after the reception here, I'm, more likely to consider it. I mean, but I'm going around the country seeing whether the message will resonate."

Asked about his timetable, Khanna told Fox News Digital, "I think starting next year people will be running."

"Imagine this, we’ve had three 80-year-old presidents in a row and suddenly you’re going to have a new generation on both sides. I think that’s fantastic for this country," he said. "I'm excited about some of the people if I do run who would be competitors. It’s going to be great. It’s going to showcase America’s talent."

With no clear frontrunner in sight, the Denver conference offered an early look at Democrats testing their messages and weighing whether to seek the party’s nomination.

item.title: Grandmother mistakes medieval gold cross for costume jewelry before learning its five-figure value
item.description: A United Kingdom grandmother nearly tossed the medieval gold reliquary cross aside as costume jewelry before fellow hobbyists confirmed it was real gold.
item.content:encoded:
A grandmother recently discovered a medieval gold cross while metal detecting in a farmer's field — and it could be worth tens of thousands of dollars.

The cross was found by 58-year-old metal detecting hobbyist Shelley Couzins in August, news agency Southwest News Service (SWNS) reported. The discovery was only recently publicized.

Couzins, a grandmother of five who took up metal detecting four years ago, told SWNS she was out with a group on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent in the United Kingdom when, after five hours of searching, she found nothing but "rubbish."

MYSTERIOUS FIND BENEATH FIELD LEADS MAN TO MASSIVE TREASURE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES

Around lunchtime, her metal detector suddenly began beeping, prompting her to dig roughly 12 inches into the freshly plowed soil.

"It was quite quiet all morning, and then I heard this beep," Couzins recalled.

She soon unearthed a gold cross — but initially dismissed it as costume jewelry.

It wasn't until she returned to the group's main tent that fellow hobbyists told her the cross was made of real gold.

REAL-LIFE EXCALIBUR? MAN ON A HIKE UNCOVERS GOLD SWORD RELIC HIDDEN UNDER TREE

"It is like a metal detectorist's dream," Couzins told SWNS. 

"You only find something like this once in a lifetime."

Couzins was searching with a group called Medway History Finders, which has withheld the field's exact location over concerns about illegal treasure hunters.

The cross, which weighs 10.6 grams, was subsequently reported to a Finds Liaison Officer under England's treasure reporting process.

MYSTERY DEEPENS AFTER 2,700-YEAR-OLD BRONZE SWORD EMERGES STANDING UPRIGHT

The grandmother said she was "absolutely gutted" about having to surrender the artifact.

"I like to keep everything I find. I know I will probably never see it again," Couzins said.

The artifact was identified as a medieval gold reliquary cross, depicting Jesus' crucifixion on one side and the Virgin Mary holding baby Jesus on the other, according to SWNS.

The cross can also be opened to hold religious relics, though Couzins said she left it sealed for fear of damaging it.

2,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE DISCOVERED BENEATH FORMER SPORTS FIELD, BREAKING REGIONAL RECORD

The artifact is being assessed by the British Museum, according to SWNS. Its ultimate ownership and value have yet to be determined.

If acquired through the treasure process, the cross would be valued, with any resulting reward expected to be split between Couzins and the landowner.

Online estimates have placed the cross's potential value at a minimum of £20,000 (roughly $27,000), though no official valuation has been announced, said SWNS.

Couzins also expressed relief that the delicate artifact had survived the plowing of the field without being destroyed.

"I really love that I saved it," she said. "If that plough had gone over again, it might have picked that up and broken it in two."

Despite her disappointment at having to give up the cross, Couzins said she hopes it will be preserved.

"I am happy for it to go to a good home, where it needs to go, instead of sitting in my cupboard."

The Isle of Sheppey has historical ties to King Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, who visited Shurland Hall on the island in October 1532, according to Historic England.

Couzins said she hopes the cross might have a connection to the royal couple, though no evidence has emerged linking the artifact to either figure.

"There are links here to Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn," she told SWNS. "We can't say it belonged to them, but that history makes this find more interesting because there could be a possibility that it is linked."

Fox News Digital reached out to Couzins for additional comment.

The discovery follows other finds of early medieval Christian artifacts across Europe in recent years.

Last year, a metal detectorist discovered a 1,200-year-old gilded Christian cross in a field in Leeds, England.

A few months later, in Germany, archaeologists reported the discovery of another Christian cross among more than 200 Viking-era artifacts dating back roughly 1,000 years.

item.title: Comedians call out Dave Chappelle over 'disgusting' routine celebrating Charlie Kirk's murder
item.description: Comedians including Rob Schneider and Tim Young condemned Dave Chappelle after leaked video showed him saying he feels better following Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.content:encoded:
Comedians Rob Schneider and Tim Young are criticizing Dave Chappelle after the veteran comic said during a New York stand-up set that he "feels better" following the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk.

The backlash follows video circulating online of Chappelle’s performance at Madison Square Garden, where he made remarks about Kirk's murder.

"I feel f---ed up saying this. It’s scary being a public speaker. And I mean, look, ever since that guy, Charlie Kirk, got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but, I feel better," Chappelle could be heard saying in the clip.

"I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling. I didn’t ask to feel this way," Chappelle said. "I just be driving around like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood? Oh!'" Chappelle continued on Friday.

CHARLAMAGNE THA GOD CALLS OUT DAVE CHAPPELLE'S KIRK COMMENTS, WOULDN'T WISH THEM 'ON MY WORST ENEMY'

On Nov 9, actor and comedian Rob Schneider wrote an open letter to Chappelle on X, accusing the comic of abandoning the compassion and openness that once defined his comedy.

"You are not the same human being you once were," Schneider said. "You are no longer a champion of compassionate freedom of thought, a person who makes people question their prejudices and preconceived judgements. An entertainer who asks their audience to open their minds and hearts more."

He added that Chappelle was now a "champion of senseless violence" and wrote, "Nobody deserves to die for engaging in conversation. And no one should ‘feel better’ after the violent murder of a husband, a father, a son and a friend."

Schneider concluded by saying he still considered Chappelle a friend and expressed hope that he would rediscover what Schneider described as the "spirit of generosity and compassion that earned you the love and respect of so many of us."

TURNING POINT USA SPOX ANDREW KOLVET SPEAKS OUT AS JENNIFER WELCH, DAVE CHAPPELLE MOCK CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER

Comedian and political commentator Tim Young also called Chappelle's remarks "disgusting," pointing to Kirk's previous defense of Chappelle after an attacker assaulted the comedian onstage at the Hollywood Bowl in 2022.

"It's actually extra disappointing to me that when Dave Chappelle was attacked on stage, Charlie Kirk was one of the first people and probably the biggest person on the right to defend Dave Chappelle and say that there shouldn't be any violence for speech," Young told Fox News Digital. "It's such a disappointing statement from Dave Chappelle now."

Young speculated that Chappelle's comments could be an effort to regain favor with the political left after years of criticism over his comedy about transgender issues.

"This might be an attempt by him to get back in the good graces of the left," Young said. "I think him making fun of Charlie Kirk's murder is, again, you're performing for this other side that you may have lost a little bit of your audience from. But at this point, Dave Chappelle is so successful and so rich, he doesn't need to perform for anybody to get there."

CHAPPELLE, JENNIFER WELCH JOKES ABOUT KIRK'S MURDER PART OF PATTERN OF LEFTISTS FINDING HUMOR IN VIOLENCE

Young also argued that comedians have become comfortable joking about violence against conservatives because they operate within politically like-minded entertainment circles.

"Mainstream comedy is very comfortable making fun of Charlie Kirk's murder because they live in a bubble," Young said. "When you get into the Hollywood bubble, when you get into the SNL bubble, you're around a bunch of liberals who agree with you. And if people disagree with you, they'll be canceled."

Fox News Digital reached out to a representative for Chappelle for comment.

Chappelle is not the only comedian to incorporate Kirk's death into his material. Former "Saturday Night Live" star Pete Davidson and current cast member Michael Che have also made jokes referencing the conservative activist's killing.

"Tony reminds me of Charlie Kirk in that he’s definitely been on camera letting a guy unload in his throat," Davidson said during Netflix’s "The Roast of Kevin Hart" in May, referring to fellow comedian Tony Hinchcliffe.

LIBERAL PODCASTERS APOLOGIZE AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT DIGGING UP CHARLIE KIRK'S BODY

Che also referenced Kirk in his Netflix special, "Michael Che: Shot in Minnesota," which premiered Oct. 13.

"I feel like Erika Kirk on this stage. That’s no disrespect to the Kirks, by the way," Che said.

The comedian said that he didn’t know who Charlie Kirk was before his death. Che joked that he initially thought people were talking about "the dude from Star Trek."

Kirk was murdered during an appearance at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025. His widow, Erika Kirk, has condemned jokes about political assassination, warning that such rhetoric reflects a broader cultural problem.

"A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay," she wrote on X. "It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together."

"You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard. Political violence must never be something this country tolerates, excuses, or celebrates," she added.

item.title: Dems' California redistricting mastermind flips script after helping party win 5 GOP seats: 'Kill'
item.description: Paul Mitchell, architect of California's Prop 50, claims Democrats should establish national standards to end partisan gerrymandering for good.
item.content:encoded:
The architect of California's Democratic-friendly redistricting plan, which helped the party flip five Republican-held House seats in November's midterm elections, is now calling on Democrats to put an end to partisan gerrymandering nationwide.

Paul Mitchell claimed in a San Francisco Chronicle op-ed published Wednesday that lawmakers should "kill partisan gerrymandering for good." His comments come after California voters approved Proposition 50 in November 2025, temporarily replacing the state's independently drawn congressional districts with a Democratic-friendly map for elections through 2030.

Mitchell acknowledged in his op-ed that Proposition 50 was designed to benefit Democrats, but defended it as a temporary response to Republican-led redistricting efforts before calling for an end to partisan mapmaking altogether.

"I wasn’t trying to do this [op-ed] to time with anyone’s efforts to do further gerrymandering," Mitchell told Fox News Digital on Thursday evening. "I always planned on doing this as soon as the election was over, and I even did a CNN interview with Elex Michaelson during the election coverage where I said that the answer needs to be to stop this redistricting war and actually fix the problem."

REDISTRICTING EFFORTS BLOW UP IN REPUBLICANS' FACES AMID HISTORIC HOUSE LOSSES

Mitchell went on to say that Prop 50 was "the right response" to Texas Republicans' redistricting push.

"Prop 50 was the right response to what Republicans in TX were doing, but recall that when TX started doing this, our approach wasn’t to just start redistricting ourselves, we did a lot of work trying to get TX to not start the redistricting wars," he told Fox News Digital. "If then someone had said "congress will be banning mid-decade redistricting" we would have been all for it. And I supported the legislation by Zoe Lofgren that would have [set up] national redistricting standards."

Mitchell argued that Republicans' midterm losses could make them more receptive to redistricting reform after years of opposing it.

"What makes now really important is that Republicans, who have opposed redistricting reform, should now realize that they lost in this war, so getting out of future wars is something maybe they would take more seriously now," he told Fox News Digital.

As for California, Mitchell believes the Proposition 50 maps will remain in place through 2030 and said the focus should be on restoring a fairer redistricting process in 2031.

He called for Congress to prohibit mid-decade redistricting but argued that such a restriction alone would not prevent partisan gerrymandering when states redraw their maps after each census.

"I think the best solution would be independent commissions in every state," he said.

The California Democratic Party touted Prop 50 as a "direct response to a Republican power grab orchestrated by President [Donald] Trump and state leaders in Texas, who redrew congressional district lines to gain five more seats in the U.S. House of Representatives."

Democratic California Gov. Gavin Newsom similarly claimed in a Nov. 4, 2025 social media post that Prop 50 "is about standing up to bullies like Donald Trump."

Mitchell's recent op-ed also claims that gerrymandering can erode voters’ ability "to elect the candidates they prefer."

Democrats notably succeeded in flipping all five House seats in California targeted by the party's redistricting push in the November midterm elections, the AP reported Nov. 4.

BLOCKBUSTER SUPREME COURT VOTING RIGHTS RULING IGNITES REDISTRICTING WAR ACROSS SOUTHERN STATES

"The incoming Congress should make national redistricting a priority, establishing minimum standards for how all states draw their districts," Mitchell wrote in the opinion piece.

Mitchell serves as the vice president of Political Data Inc., a California-based bipartisan voter data firm. He is also the owner of Redistricting Partners, a Sacramento-based data consulting firm.

Mitchell, across his career, has conducted more than 100 redistrictings for states, cities, school boards and community college districts, including the State of New York Independent Redistricting Commission, the Los Angeles City Council Redistricting Commission and the Long Beach Independent Redistricting Commission, according to Redistricting Partners' website.

When asked about whether California's gerrymandered maps were necessary during a Nov. 8 interview on "California Politics 360," Mitchell said it would have been "a huge mistake" for Democrats to "sit" on their "laurels."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Following Democrats' sweeping victories in November's midterm elections, some states have floated redrawing their congressional maps ahead of the 2028 election cycle, Roll Call reported Nov. 9.

Meanwhile, outgoing Republican Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp said Nov. 4 that he would not call a special legislative session to redraw congressional maps or limit the powers of the incoming governor before his term ends in January 2027, WABE reported.

"As long as I’m governor, we will always respect the results of secure, accessible, and fair elections, and also abide by the laws and constitution of our state," Kemp said in a statement.

Here's the real kicker: Lazishvili has now been ADDED to Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi card at Etihad Arena in the United Arab Emirates. The Georgian will actually replace Umar Nurmagomedov and will reportedly face UFC legend Urijah Faber.

Amazing.

As for Nurmagomedov ... he's currently facing six months in prison after Wednesday's attack, and will also have to pay an $82,000 fine and be ordered to deportation following his prison term. Dvalishvili has since said he doesn't want to press charges.

Industry insiders believe Wednesday's attack stems from UFC 311 back in January 2025. Dvalishvili defended his bantamweight title via unanimous decision, and the two traded barbs ever since.

Seems like Dvalishvili may have gotten the last laugh, though ...

At least for a few months.

item.title: Anti-Trump Republican courts other defectors as House weighs another vote against Iran war
item.description: Thomas Massie says he's offering Republicans a "life boat from MAGA" as he pushes a new Iran War Powers resolution to the House floor soon..
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: House Republicans and Democrats are preparing another effort to challenge President Donald Trump's military operations in Iran, with lawmakers signaling that additional Republicans could break with the president and support a War Powers resolution.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., told Fox News Digital that another Iran War Powers resolution could come to the House floor "in the next few legislative days" or around Christmas.

This would mark the fourth attempt this year to restrict Trump's military actions against Iran.

"I'm offering Republicans a life boat from MAGA," Massie told Fox News Digital, expressing optimism that more members of his party could join the effort.

7 REPUBLICANS REBEL AGAINST TRUMP, VOTE WITH DEMS TO REIN IN IRAN WAR POWERS

House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers, R-Ala., told Fox News Digital that he would oppose the resolution but acknowledged that "Massie has been having conversations with members" in an effort to secure additional Republican support.

Rep. Jeff Van Drew, R-N.J., echoed Rogers' assessment, suggesting that "one or two" additional Republicans could join Massie and the Democrats who previously supported the measure.

SWING-DISTRICT REPUBLICAN BREAKS WITH TRUMP, PUSHES LIMITS ON IRAN WAR

Reps. Tom Barrett, R-Mich., Warren Davidson, R-Ohio, and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., previously voted in favor of an Iran War Powers resolution.

Barrett told Fox News Digital on Thursday that he would maintain his support if the new resolution mirrors the previous legislation.

"My position would be consistent for it," Barrett said.

However, Barrett expressed skepticism that additional Republicans would join the effort, noting that few members appeared willing to shift their positions during the previous vote.

GOP HOLDS WITH TRUMP ON IRAN WAR, BUT CRACKS EMERGE AS DEADLINE NEARS

Massie also acknowledged uncertainty over whether he could secure more Republican votes, criticizing his party's continued support for Trump's military operations.

"Congress is paralyzed," Massie told Fox News Digital, accusing Republicans of remaining "still in the suicide pact with this administration."

TRUMP SUFFERS RARE HOUSE DEFEAT AS BIPARTISAN VOTE MOVES TO WITHDRAW TROOPS FROM IRAN CONFLICT

House Democrats, meanwhile, expressed optimism that Republicans' losses in the 2026 midterm elections could encourage more GOP lawmakers to break with Trump's foreign policy agenda.

"If they're listening to the people that sent them here, yes," Rep. Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., told Fox News Digital when asked whether additional Republicans could support the effort. "That's what they should do."

Rep. Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., also expressed confidence that more Republicans could join the effort, saying she "thinks they would."

Meanwhile, Rep. Adelita Grijalva, D-Ariz., suggested that Republicans may feel less pressure to remain aligned with Trump following the midterm elections — especially as many prepare to leave Congress and others hunker down to serve in the minority.

"The threat of Trump dumping a lot of money into Republican districts is over, perhaps more members of Congress we think represent their communities will listen to what constituents are saying about the war," Grijalva told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP PLEDGES TO VETO 'INSANE' DEM BILLS, PINPOINTS ISSUE PARTIALLY TO BLAME FOR REPUBLICAN LOSSES

The renewed effort comes as lawmakers continue debating Congress' constitutional authority over military operations and the president's ability to conduct sustained hostilities without congressional authorization.

Under the Constitution, Congress holds the power to declare war, while the president serves as commander in chief of the armed forces. The War Powers Resolution of 1973 establishes procedures and limits for military operations conducted without congressional authorization.

Despite growing discussions among lawmakers, no vote on an Iran War Powers resolution has been scheduled or confirmed.

item.title: Florida Republican on Democrats' strategy: 'That's the choice they have to make...persecution or policy'
item.description: Controversial Florida congressman charges Democrats will choose to pursue persecution over policy, but also signals willingness to compromise, given the right conditions.
item.content:encoded:
Florida's Rep. Randy Fine has a blunt prescription for a House Republican conference staring down a steep Democratic majority in January: stop worrying about compromise, hand the minority gavel to Rep. Jim Jordan, and start fighting, suggesting that Democrats will likely pursue political persecution as the main focus in the next Congress.

In a wide-ranging interview with Fox News Digital, Fine—who expanded his own victory margin to 19 points even as Republicans lost control of the chamber—argued that voters punished the GOP not for its policies, but because they didn't see lawmakers willing to go to the mat for them.

‘HE BLAMED THE JEWS’: GOP CONGRESSMAN LEVELS EXPLOSIVE ACCUSATION AGAINST JD VANCE OVER ELECTION POSTMORTEM

For Fine, the message sent by Jordan's election is unambiguous:

"Well, it says to me that we're ready to fight back. I mean, Jim Jordan has two unique qualifications for the job. 

"One, he's our best fighter. He protected and fought for President Trump during the ridiculous impeachments of President Trump's first term. He's just somebody who knows how to go into the arena and fight back. 

"But the second thing is, he's an extraordinary communicator. And over the next two years, we are in a very diminished minority. That's going to be our greatest strength, is to point out why the Democratic policies won't actually improve anyone's lives, and to point out the policies that we would propose that will. So, as a fighter and a communicator, I think he's very well positioned to lead us for the next two years."

Fine downplays policy as the primary driver of the disastrous 2026 blue tsunami:

"I don't know that we need to change our policies. And I don't even know how much of our messaging we need to change. What we need to do is we need to fight. I believe that we lost the election because voters thought we didn't care about their problems, because they didn't see us fighting to solve them. 

"Voters will vote for you if they see you fighting, even if you fail. But they won't vote for you if they don't see you fighting. Now I'm a guy who defied the odds. I increased my margin in the election. I may be the only Republican in the country to do that. I won my last election by 14, I won this one by 19."

With House Republicans shifting from passing bills to playing defense after electing Rep. Jim Jordan to succeed outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson as minority leader, Fine drew a sharp line between the two leadership roles.

"Well, it's a very different job. Look, I think if we kept the majority, I think Mike Johnson would still be the speaker. The speaker's job and the minority leader's job are completely different. So Mike Johnson's job for the next 50 plus days is to try to get as many good things passed through the House as he can. 

FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM'

"Jim Jordan's not going to be able to pass anything. The Democrats could have a 90 to 100 vote majority. His job is going to be to fight back when they're impeaching and they're interrogating and they are being vindictive, but also again to communicate why their policies will not make people's lives better. 

"They're going to come out and say Medicare for all. We're going to have to say, 'No, no there's no such thing. It's going to be Medicaid for all. When you give it to everyone, everyone will suffer. We'll end up like Canada where there are death panels or the UK where you can wait a year or two to get to a doctor.' That's what we're going to have to do: fight back and communicate. That's a very different job than what Mike Johnson had to do the last two years."

Gridlock may be the persistent feature of the next Congress, but Fine does not completely discard the potential for compromise:

"Well, first off, compromise isn't inevitable. We may not do very much for the next two years. And I think that's the most likely outcome. Democrats pass ridiculous things, President Trump vetoes them, and then we uphold the veto in the House and the Senate. I think that's the most likely outcome for the next two years. 

"If it relates to compromise, you have to see what we're offered. So, for example, if Democrats would agree to voter ID, which is a huge thing the American people want, they might be able to extract a concession from us. If they're willing to stop so much of the ridiculous immigration into this country, they might be able to get concessions from us on other things. So, the problem is this: to Democrats, compromise means we give them what they want. It's always a one-way street. 

"It's funny, when Democrats win, they say elections have consequences. When we win, they say we need to be bipartisan. And that's how their viewpoint is. They never come to our side of the world. So I'll see if they want to compromise. I'll be open to it. But it will truly require us getting some of the things that we want that they have fought us on for the time I've been in Congress."

On foreign policy objectives, Fine points to several Democrats he's prepared to work with, while clarifying his position on Israel:

"Sure. I mean, look, in the Senate, you've got John Fetterman, who I think is an incredibly strong advocate for Western civilization. I don't think it's fair to say I'm an advocate for Israel. That makes it sound like I'm just an advocate for a country. It's more than that. 

"The United States and Israel are the only two countries in the world that are unambiguously standing up to Muslim terror, which seeks to fundamentally redefine life for all of us around the world. So I'm on the side of Western civilization and John Fetterman embodies that in the Senate. I think you've got guys like Jared Moskowitz and Josh Gottheimer on the House side, on the Democratic side, who do as well…Unfortunately, I think they're pretty outnumbered at this point, but if they want to fight with me, I'm happy to fight alongside them."

Finally, Fine contends that the Democrats face a clear dichotomy in how they want to proceed to govern, but argues they will likely make the wrong choice:

"The American people elected Democrats not because they wanted investigations and persecution. They elected Democrats because they didn't think we were solving their problems. If they make the mistake of going down the vengeance and persecution path, they'll end up in two years just the same way we did. If they try to solve the problems of the American people, they'll do well. 

"The problem is their ideas don't work. Remember, the Affordable Care Act didn't make health care affordable. But if they try to do things that will help the American people, at least they'll be listening to them. But that's the choice they have to make. Persecution or policy. I think they're going to choose persecution, but we'll find out in a couple of months."

item.title: Jayden Maiava and Josh Hoover face off as USC visits defending national champion Indiana
item.description: USC's Jayden Maiava faces Josh Hoover and Indiana in a College Football Playoffs-relevant clash, but the Hoosiers' four straight close games raise doubts.
item.content:encoded:
There has been some news about College Football recently about the idea that they are expanding to 24 teams in the College Football Playoffs. That won’t happen this year, but it will next season. If that were the case, it is likely that both of these teams would be part of that. There are a lot of people complaining because it likely will take away Conference Tournaments. Personally, I like the expansion. Before we get there, let’s take a look at today’s game between USC and Indiana.

USC is 7-2 for the season, and they are 20th in the nation coming into this afternoon’s game. The Trojans' losses came against Oregon and Wisconsin this season. The Oregon loss is probably the most frustrating because they were at home, and the Ducks haven’t been consistently good this season. The loss on the road against Wisconsin was a bit confusing as well. The Trojans should’ve been plenty good to beat the Badgers, but they couldn’t get anything going on the ground to open things up. Their leading rusher in the game had 28 yards on the ground.

You can’t really blame the running game completely; I think we all know the Trojans will only go as far as quarterback Jayden Maiava will take them. He has completed about 67% of passes this year and thrown for 20 touchdowns. He only has five interceptions this season, so he has put together a good year. He had two interceptions against Wisconsin, which clearly didn’t help the USC cause. He also somehow had -57 rushing yards in the Wisconsin game.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL SELLS ANOTHER PIECE OF ITS SOUL WITH CFP OFFICIALLY EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS

Indiana is the defending National Champion, but the team that won last year is significantly different from this season’s team. Fernando Mendoza is obviously gone, and the team was going to have to adjust to him leaving for the NFL. They don’t have a bad quarterback – Josh Hoover – under center, it just is that he isn’t quite as elite as Mendoza. Hoover has fewer than 2,000 yards this season, but he does have 19 touchdown passes. Perhaps the best part is that he is taking care of the ball, throwing just two interceptions this season.

The Hoosiers haven’t looked very good lately, either. Perhaps they are playing better competition than before, but they’ve had four consecutive close games. They won by just three against Nebraska. Then they lost by four to Ohio State, though they probably could’ve won that game if they could’ve stayed in bounds. Then they had to go into overtime to beat Michigan. The following week, they again needed overtime in order to beat Minnesota. Four straight weeks of close games, but the team went 3-1.

INDIANA SURVIVES MINNESOTA SCARE WITH SECOND STRAIGHT OVERTIME WIN TO KEEP NATIONAL TITLE DEFENSE ALIVE

This could be a great game between the two teams, and I find it very hard to trust Indiana right now. Both teams are coming off of bye weeks, so they have had plenty of time to prepare for this game. I think Indiana has the better defense, and I do think they likely took this time to get their team refocused. I’m going to take the Hoosiers here, but I’m going to play them at just -7 instead of them at -7.5.

item.title: College football legend Brian Bosworth says he supports the controversial 24-team expanded playoff
item.description: College Football great Brian Bosworth said he likes the new College Football Playoff format as it gives more programs an opportunity to showcase themselves.
item.content:encoded:
College football legend Brian Bosworth is a fan of the controversially expanded playoff format.

The 24-team format will begin in the 2027–28 season and run for five seasons, but fans don’t like it because it dilutes the impact of the regular season. However, Bosworth likes the new format because it gives more programs opportunities to compete on bigger stages.

"It just gets bigger and better, and it deserves to be bigger and better because there's so many college programs that deserve the opportunity to show who they are," Bosworth told OutKick in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Oklahoma football legend talked about the incredible parity in college football and how top teams lose nearly every weekend . Bosworth also said the expanded playoff gives more fans a reason to stay invested later into the season.

"To expand to include colleges that otherwise would be forgotten. They're on the edge and you say, ‘Oh, maybe next year, maybe next year.’ It gives the fans some more hope. It gives them a dream. It gives them a destination and it keeps their passion alive," Bosworth said.

When asked whether 24 teams realistically have a chance to win the national championship each season, Bosworth said not to discount the longshots.

"There could be 10 or 12 really good teams, but there could be another 10 teams behind them that are just hungry and want an opportunity. So, yeah, it extends the season and it gives more teams an opportunity, but there's something to be said about the long shot or the hungry dog," Bosworth said.

RAVENS STAR KYLE HAMILTON SAYS HE HATES WHERE COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS GOING AMID 24-TEAM PLAYOFF, NIL CHAOS

Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is returning to the Bulldogs next season on a $7.5 million deal that could reach $9 million with incentives, according to multiple reports. Bosworth has said the exorbitant amounts of money involved in some of these contracts are a "head-scratcher."

"The money has gotten to a point where it's just a head scratcher. I'm a firm believer of putting some fences around it and controlling the fact that not every school is going to have the deep pockets in which to go deep into," Bosworth said.

"I think the fairness of it should be across the board that every team has the same pool so that they can manage the team across the board. Everybody's doing the same thing on the same page and you don't have somebody that's funneling money into it and then you can have these crazy contracts the way they're going about it now."

Bosworth noted that Taylor is an amazing player, but football isn’t a one-man show. If the team doesn’t invest in the players around him, it will struggle to play well.

"But it's not a one-man show (because) great quarterbacks can fail based upon their offensive scheme, the play calling, the injuries on the offensive line. If you've got a defense that's super porous, you know. It really does take a team to be an elite team to get into the conversation to be a championship in the conference and then maybe get to the playoffs," Bosworth said.

Bosworth knows what it takes to have a winning team, as he won the 1985 national championship and three Big Eight titles. He won the Butkus Award as the nation’s top linebacker in both 1985 and 1986. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2015.

In addition to being a star linebacker during his playing days, Bosworth has also brought the iconic "Sheriff Boz" to life in Dr Pepper commercials. In Norman, Oklahoma, Dr Pepper is bringing Fansville to life with the Dr Pepper Water Tower Park.

More than a landmark, the park gives fans a new gathering place to connect, celebrate gameday traditions and experience a piece of Fansville . Bosworth, who knows the passion of Oklahoma fans well, said bringing Fansville to life is a dream come true.

"It's really a dream come true," Bosworth, who spoke on behalf of Dr Pepper said. "College football is perpetual. It's been with us, it's here now and it will always be with us. And to be part of that is really an honor. And to have Fansville come here and then put up their iconic water tower in a spot, it's just cherry. You couldn't ask for anything better."

item.title: Ben Shapiro warns Democrats have 'strong incentive' to crater the economy and blame Trump

Democrats could be gearing up to undermine the economy and leave President Donald Trump to shoulder the blame, Daily Wire co-founder Ben Shapiro warned this week, raising concerns about the party's agenda following its 2026 midterm victories.

"I think that the Democrats right now have a strong incentive to basically crater the American economy over the course of the next two years and blame President Trump for it," Shapiro told Sean Hannity on the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

Shapiro predicted that Democrats would introduce "affordability bills" that "aren't actually about affordability" and seek to "destroy" the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, as part of what he characterized as a broader effort to undermine Trump's presidency.

DEMOCRATS SAY THEY'LL MAKE LIFE AFFORDABLE. YOUR WALLET MAY DISAGREE

The warning comes after Democrats' midterm victories, which Shapiro suggested could embolden the party to pursue a more aggressive legislative agenda.

"And they'll do it in the name of populism," he said.

During Thursday's podcast episode, Shapiro also discussed his evolving views on Trump, the rise of antisemitism, the personal security threats he says have affected his family and his outlook on the 2028 presidential race.

CONSERVATIVES STUNNED BY 'CATASTROPHIC' MIDTERM BLUE TSUNAMI, BLAME TRUMP'S IRAN WAR, HIGH GAS PRICES

"The only hope that Republicans have is that Democrats will do what Democrats typically do, which is misread the moment, see this as a mandate for radical change..." Shapiro said, discussing Republicans' prospects following the midterm elections.

"You and I have been in this game for a long time, and we've seen a lot of these cycles," he told Hannity.

"And whenever I hear Republicans go, 'Oh, we'll never win again,' I'm old enough to remember when Barack Obama won re-election and then four years later, Donald Trump was taking his seat in the Oval Office," he added.

Viewers can watch or listen to Sean Hannity's full conversation with Ben Shapiro on the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast, available on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and iHeartRadio.

item.title: WWE champion wants no part of the John Cena Classic
item.description: Ethan Page explains why he refuses to enter the John Cena Classic, saying WWE fans would vote against him no matter how dominant his performance.
item.content:encoded:
John Cena’s namesake pro wrestling showcase will feature some of the best WWE has to offer and give the fans a voice in who takes home a championship belt next month.

Ethan Page, who won the Intercontinental Championship earlier this month over Chad Gable, said he wants no part in it – at least for right now.

"I think it's silly for you to think that I, as the smartest wrestler in the WWE, would put me in a position that even if I defeat my opponent, I could not win because of the voting fans, who boo me out of every single building that I walk into, and now I'm gonna put the power of my success, on a device where no one has to look me in the eye and tell me that they don't appreciate what I offer," Page told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview.

"They get to hide in a bathroom stall, or even worse, surround themselves with like-minded idiots. They will all decide that I am not worthy of their vote and then, at the end of this event, some pathetic crybaby who went on a political tour on social media for seven weeks straight, gets voted into victory and my talents are completely ignored. Never mind my talents, my more than likely victory, over some poor schmuck from NXT, will go unrewarded."

WWE fans will get the power to vote for the winner of the John Cena Classic via Club WWE. The winner will get to take home the John Cena Classic Championship.

And, yes, the wrestlers in the competition don’t necessarily have to win their match to win the title.

Page did clarify, saying he’s happy those in the competition could get an accolade they could be proud of and if he was invited, maybe he would reconsider.

"Now let me answer politically correct. I'm happy that people will get the opportunity to have something in their career they can be proud of," he added. "The only issue is I already do. I am the intercontinental champion, and I am not going to rush to get in line for a free watch and a jacket with another man's name on it, so I can enter a tournament that I will be voted to lose, no matter what.

"Now if I get invited, we'll talk about it then and I will reassess my decisions, but at this very moment, that is my clear-cut stance on the John Cena Classic, and I wish everybody luck. And I hope they manipulate the fan base enough to vote for them, so that they can win and be happy."

The John Cena Classic will take place at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex at Disney World on Dec. 14. It will be a part of a special double episode of "Monday Night Raw" – the first of which is taking place in Australia following Wrestlepalooza: Perth.
